promptState.text: Turn this summer photo into a snowy winter evening. Cover the roof, the terrace, the wall tops and the plants with fresh snow, make the sky a deep evening blue, and add warm yellow light glowing in the window. Keep the house, the blue door, the wicker armchair and the camera angle exactly as they are.

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - The picture you are editing. The result keeps its shape.
  • 2. Output Size - How many pixels the result has: 1024, about 1 megapixel, the size a 6 GB card can finish. The note on the right says why there is no bigger one. Your picture keeps its shape.
  • 3. Add a prompt - What to change, and what to keep. With one picture there is no tag to name: just describe the picture.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your picture and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note on the right says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the exact size the model uses at the Output Size you picked: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in your picture's shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales your picture to that size and crops the few pixels that do not fit, so the model edits a picture exactly the size of the result. Nothing is stretched, and the result lines up with your picture in the Compare.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and your picture. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes it as it comes, already sized by the helpers. It also makes the blank canvas for the result at that size, which is why there is no separate latent node. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Your picture and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 720, "height": 1259, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this version is for

This is the Qwen Image 2.1 One Image Edit workflow, set up for graphics cards with 6 GB of memory. It edits your picture the same way, following your prompt: here, the summer terrace turned into a snowy winter evening. The result keeps your picture's shape, and what you do not ask to change stays as it was.

Only the Output Size list is different: this version offers 1024, about 1 megapixel, the size a 6 GB card can finish, and leaves out 1536 and Qwen's native 2K (the part below says why).

Every number below was measured on a 6 GB RTX 2060 in a PC with 64 GB of memory, with this workflow and its own settings.

 How long a Run takes

Output SizeResultNew picture or promptNew seed only
1024 - about 1 MP1024 x 10241 min 47 sabout 1 min 35 s

The result size is for a square picture like the demo one. Change the picture or the prompt and the model reads the picture again, which is the first time column. Change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second.

The first Run after starting ComfyUI took 1 min 59 s, because it also loads the 6.8 GB image model and the 8.7 GB text encoder.

 Why there is no 1536 or 2K

At 1536 the card ran out of its own memory at step 1 of 25, and Windows moved the work into the computer's memory, which is far slower. The Run then stopped moving, and the stop button could not end it: only closing ComfyUI did. 2048 needs more memory still, so both are left out. For bigger pictures, use the normal workflow on a card with more memory.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

While it renders, the model keeps what it has worked out about your picture and the prompt in a cache, so it does not redo that on every step. The teal node says where that cache lives. Leave it on auto / default.

On this card all four settings took about the same time, each at 1024 with a new seed only, on the same seed:

SettingTimeThe picture
auto / default (as set)1 min 36 s-
cpu / default1 min 31 sexactly the same
auto / int81 min 31 spractically the same
cpu / int81 min 27 spractically the same

None of them is faster here: a few seconds is the normal spread between two Runs (the same setting took 1 min 32 s and 1 min 36 s). What dtype int8 does change is the computer's memory: ComfyUI used about 20 GB with it, against 23 GB without. If your computer is short on memory, set it to int8.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention. On this card it made each step more than twice as fast: 3.6 s a step at 1024, against 7.9 s with the normal pytorch attention, so 1 min 36 s against 3 min 41 s for a Run on the same seed. The two pictures came out practically the same.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 What it takes

The graphics card peaked at about 5.4 GB of its 6 GB during these runs, counting the part Windows and the browser hold. The models wait in the computer's memory while the card works through them: ComfyUI used about 23 GB of it.

 Why the picture is trimmed a little

The model works in steps of 32 pixels, and most pictures do not divide evenly. Qwen's text encoder on its own stretches the picture to the nearest size that does, by up to about 2 percent (0.9 percent on a 4:3 photo), and the result then comes out slightly wider or narrower than your picture. Here the helpers crop instead of stretching: a thin strip, usually a few pixels, comes off two opposite edges, and the result keeps the exact proportions and lines up in the Compare.

 Writing the prompt

  • Say what should change and what should stay: the demo ends with Keep the house, the blue door, the wicker armchair and the camera angle exactly as they are.
  • Describe the change concretely: where the snow lies, the colour of the sky, which lights glow.
  • To type only a short request and let the node write the full prompt, use workflow 5. To change one small area and keep every other pixel, use workflow 3 (Inpaint). To bring in a second picture, like an outfit or a logo, see the Multi Image Edit folder.

On this card, on 5 seeds: every one kept the house, the blue door, the armchair and the camera angle, and turned the terrace into a snowy evening with a lit window.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1499, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
